# Production-response regressions

`ppt-qwen-owner-topology.json` preserves the source-ID dispositions and ten-page ownership topology of an actual qwen3.8-max response from 2026-10-20. It intentionally contains unowned visible summaries. Source prose, credentials and account data are omitted. The regression must reject its incomplete contract instead of silently expanding 61 explicitly owned units to 168.

`ppt-qwen-table-projection.json` preserves one actual malformed table projection with a missing selected row. Repair must retain the selected original rows, columns and ownership; a smaller table is not a valid fallback.

`ppt-qwen-outline-first-factor-zoo.json` preserves the outline-first planning replies of one actual qwen3.8-max Factor Zoo run from 2026-10-21 (182 source units, body language `both`, Process Improvement native template, adaptive target 12 / max 16). It keeps the model's own card and page titles, source-ID ownership, dispositions and allocation reasons; source prose and summaries are omitted (the inventory keeps only id, type, language pair, length and table row count). It contains: a semantic outline without a cover; one missing the bilingual introduction pair; one repaired by the actual coverage reply; a capacity allocation with an empty table-continuation page; two 16-page allocations whose long or ID-citing reason masked a missing last topic; the accepted 11-page allocation; and page materializations that exclude translations under `body: both`, before and after the specific retry feedback. `selftest-ppt-outline-first-replay.mjs` must detect each original failure and accept only through the bounded repair paths. The later summary/coverage review chain needs source text, so its passes, failures and coverage conflicts are recorded as data, not replayed. `editorialAllocation` keeps the actual editorial-allocation reply that crossed reviewed topics (topics 1 and 2 merged on page 1, topics 3–6 moved one page forward, topics 7 and 8 mixed). It was saved as both repair checkpoints and made every "continue repair" fail. The replay asserts that the reply is rejected when applied, with the crossing source IDs, and that the poisoned checkpoints are skipped on resume. `retryChain` keeps the eight scoped repair passes of the real retry on `7bb1fdbf` and its final model-judged coverage failure (14 source IDs); `selftest-ppt-outline-governor.mjs` replays it through the phase-A governor (one repair per judged kind, then an advisory; repair budget; oscillation). `languageFallback` keeps the scripts (not the prose) of the four bilingual summaries left by the real retry on `0f04a5b4` (b_0060–b_0063, two language pairs; repairs wrote both languages into each summary) and its three repair passes; the replay asserts the deterministic fallback shows both pairs as original text on the same page and leaves everything else unchanged. `topicKept` keeps the real editorial-selection batch delta from the retry on `98cf5ff7` that excluded b_0222/b_0223, the only visible units of the major topic "14. Summary" (section path, unit types and states only); the replay builds the same batch through `editorialSelectionTasks`, asserts it is rejected at apply time with those IDs and the topic, and that the fallback keeps the topic visible on its page. `proseWindows` keeps the shapes (IDs and field lengths, no prose) of the ten real `editorial-prose-cells` window replies from the retry on `1ec4a029`: six exceeded the private planning-field limits while every summaryText was valid; the replay asserts the exact field errors, one correction retry per window, trimming the private planning fields (all ten replies then apply), one correction retry for a reply invalid in its content, dropping a window that stays invalid, and that the other windows still apply. `budgetRun` keeps the stage names of every model call of the retry on `d6422842` (25 charges under the old metering) and its editorial-reduction reply that excluded b_0222/b_0223; the governor selftest asserts only repair-loop passes are charged, and the replay asserts the reduction is rejected with those IDs, retried once, then dropped. `loadModel` keeps the measured full-width heights of every owned source unit on the template's largest native content layout (inches only, no prose), the body sizes of all 7 content layouts (capacity = their mean area, independent of the page schedule) and the accepted standard plan's stacked height (115.3 in) that the C1 load factors are calibrated on; the replay reproduces the production estimate (concise 26 / standard 32 / detailed 43 pages), asserts C1 asks the author when 16 pages are authorized, and C2 splits the real 11-page allocation into same-topic continuation pages within the maximum. `capacity.tailDropped22` is the real 22-page allocation (concise, max 22) that left out b_0222–b_0224 of the approved last topic; the replay asserts they now join that topic's last page (a missing language partner joins its partner's page), only the public reason then remains for the reason-only repair, a topic without pages still fails, and C2 splits after completion when the maximum leaves room. `languageFallback.preempted` keeps the trace of the re-plan on `d5773b81` where a returning source-language failure (b_0166) hit the oscillation stop before its deterministic fallback; the replay asserts the fallback now runs first, even after a stop, and that no model repair follows. `emptyPage` keeps the structure (no prose) of the last valid checkpoint and the failing candidate of the 32-page re-plan on `93e2cf88`, where a repair moved page 16's only sources onto page 15 of the same topic; the replay asserts the gate now reports an empty page, the page is dropped (31 pages, later references renumbered, droppedPageIds recorded), and that excluded, cross-topic, still-referenced or fixed-count cases are kept. `tableFallback` keeps the shape of table b_0016 (size, numeric cell positions) and of the two real editorial-selection replies that rewrote its condensed cells against the projection rules (row indices, error, changed-cell positions and kinds; no cell text); the replay rebuilds both with placeholder cells, asserts each reproduces its real violation, that the trace names the table, and that the original cells of the selected rows are restored deterministically on the second failure, also after a stop. `editorialEmptyPage` keeps the 31-page checkpoint (structure only) and the real exclusions of page 8 ("CAPM Testable Predictions") from the re-plan on `c42d78fc`; the replay asserts the page is dropped when its topic keeps other pages (30 pages), that a topic's last page is never dropped, and that a batch emptying it is rejected at apply time with the IDs and kept by the fallback. `proseMediaFallback` keeps the shape (offsets, quote lengths and true positions; no text) of the relation graphs every real editorial-selection reply gave b_0214/b_0215 on `70f28e8e`, and their state before the round; the replay rebuilds them on placeholder text and asserts the real offsets fail while exact ones pass, the batch is rejected at apply time with both IDs, the previous entries (original objects) are restored after the retry, and the repair loops show the original objects after one failed repair, also after a stop. `bilingualSplit` keeps the error and IDs of the batch on `8884eb14` that split the "14. Summary" pair b_0222/b_0223 on both tries; the replay asserts the pair is named for the correction retry, keeps its previous entries (both languages visible) when it stays split, and that a batch still invalid under a rule that names no sources is skipped rather than failing the run. `obligationKept` keeps the structure of batch 8 of the cassette run `run_6e3a2c96` on cd5a2737 (the 12 units of section 2.5 on one page, their destinations before and in the reply, the obligation "FF5 dividend discount motivation" with its trigger, placement and evidence offsets; no text); the replay rebuilds the obligation on placeholder text and asserts the real reply is rejected at apply time naming b_0117, passes apply without the check and then fails the gate as it did live, keeps the b_0117/b_0118 pair's previous summaries on the participants' page after the correction, leaves obligations that were already incomplete to earlier rounds, and that editorial reduction carries the same guard.

## Run cassettes (offline replay of a whole run)

The fixtures above replay one function at a time. A run cassette replays the whole orchestration of one run (repair loops, governor, fallbacks, batches, drops) without a model call. The lab service (`scripts/ppt/manual-test-service.mjs`) records, for every model call, success or failure, a version-2 record in `model-responses/`: `seq` (process order), `runId` and `runSeq`, `commit` (`sha`, `backendDirty`, loaded-code `codeHash`), stage key, prompt hash and length (never the prompt), options, timing and the reply or the error (`code`, `modelStage`, `diagnostic`, bounded details; keys redacted). Before each POST project action it copies the stored project and the request body to `request-snapshots/`, kept only when the action started a run: a run rewrites the audit caches and selection marks it starts from, so its start state exists only there.

`node scripts/ppt/build-cassette.mjs --live <dir> --run <runId>` joins the snapshot with the run's calls, outcome (status, failure code, step, trace class, source IDs, governor stop), event types and template files into `outputs/ppt-cassettes/<project>-<runId>/`. `node apps/cowork-server/selftest-ppt-cassette.mjs` replays a cassette in a temporary state root: the recorded request goes through `handlePpt`, calls are served by stage key and occurrence, and the run must reach the recorded outcome and event counts with no missing call (the code asks for a call the recording lacks), no unused call (a recorded call is no longer made); prompt drift is reported (`PPT_CASSETTE_TRACE=1` prints a timeline). Replies of parallel calls are released in their recorded completion order: some code merges parallel results as they finish (on `run_6e3a2c96`, `auditEditorialSummaries` collects summary conflicts from three concurrent windows in completion order, so serving them in start order changed the next `outline:summary:9` prompt and its reply no longer applied). If the code never makes a call that finished earlier live, a watchdog releases the waiting replies after 5 s of idle event loop and names them in `orderBroken`. After an intended change, the selftest's `EXPECTATIONS` table says, per recorded run, what the replay must show instead of the recorded outcome; a correction retry the change adds can be served the batch's recorded first reply (`repeatFirstAttempt`, the model repeating itself). For `run_6e3a2c96`, at the obligation fix (`57f676ea`) the replay served all 57 recorded calls without drift, sent batch 8 back for its correction, kept b_0117/b_0118, completed the selection and stopped past the recorded failure at the first summary audit the live run never reached. Since summary conflicts are listed in source order (they came in network order live, and the summary repair takes the first 12), the replay ends at `outline:summary:9`, the first prompt built from them: 16 calls unchanged, then the recorded reply no longer fits. A recording made after a change like this is the new baseline. The baseline after both fixes is `cd5a2737-run_36648dc2…` (recorded on `82b693f9`): 76 calls replay exactly to its failure at editorial allocation. With several cassettes the selftest replays each in its own process (the store reads its state root once per process). At the allocation completion the baseline serves all 76 calls, completes the corrected allocation (b_0168 listed twice), finds that it also crosses reviewed topics (b_0187/b_0188/b_0168), drops it through the topic-conflict path and continues to prose-cell windows the live run never reached. `7976bd9a-run_c5dbf940…` is the first 12_ml_quant expand (concise, max 45): both capacity replies left six of twelve topics without pages and split the b_0084/b_0085 pair. Stage keys of planning requests embed a random request revision (`outline:capacity:<revision>`), so a cassette stores the run's revision and the player maps the replay's own revision onto it. Capacity is now allocated per topic with page quotas set by code from the measured loads, so this recording's whole-deck calls are no longer made; a stand-in returns unparsable output for each per-topic call, every topic is packed by measured height (quotas 4, 2, 7, 2, 5, 3, 5, 4, 4, 1, 7 plus the cover: 45 pages), the plan passes the deck acceptance and the run continues to page materialization. `7976bd9a-run_a6128e0e…` is the per-topic capacity acceptance run (capacity and all 44 materializations passed) that then failed on a 245-character internal `reason` (b_0208); with internal reasons trimmed, 62 calls replay without drift and the repair loop goes on into a step the recording lacks. First cassette: `cd5a2737-run_6e3a2c96…` (standard, max 32, recorded on `34810de7`): 57 calls replay offline to the recorded failure (`coverage_invalid` at `outline:editorial-local:selection`, b_0117/b_0119/b_0120, oscillation) in 6-9 minutes; the time is the pipeline's own local work (262 of the 649 live seconds had no model call in flight). Cassettes contain source text and model replies, so they stay under the git-ignored `outputs/`; without one the real replay is skipped and only the synthetic recorder/player checks run.
